verdict: Do A plus a narrow form of B: make `_prune_stale` report every claim it drops to stderr (id/role/work-item/files/resources/age) on claim, list and release, and add a floor to `--stale-after-seconds` enforced only in `main()`'s argument validation (reject anything below ~300s with an error naming the value passed), leaving the library functions' parameter unbounded so existing direct-call tests keep passing. Everything else — deleting `_owner_alive`, redesigning liveness, adding a `--force` override — is scope creep; report it, don't build it.
reasoning: Evidence 3 and 4 are two distinct failure links and each needs its own two-line fix. Loudness alone (A) only converts silent destruction into visible destruction: the agent in evidence 4 had already concluded 'stale' and chose to prune, so a stderr line gives it evidence to report but does not stop the take. A floor alone (B) blocks that exact accident but leaves the 24h default path still deleting live-lane claims with no trace, which is the same silent-corruption class agents.md singles out as worse than a lane overstepping to fix a tool. Together they are the whole minimal repair and neither changes claim semantics. Option C is partly wrong as stated: `_owner_alive` is also called from `_exclusive_lock`, where the pid genuinely belongs to a still-running process, so deleting the function breaks stale-lock recovery; only the conjunct inside `_prune_stale` is dead, and removing it is a behavioural no-op for real claims (evidence 1) that would break `test_stale_claim_is_pruned_when_owner_is_gone` (evidence 5) while unblocking nothing. Correcting the `--stale-after-seconds` help text and the `_prune_stale` docstring to say pruning is age-only is the honest part of C and costs nothing; do that, keep the function. The floor must live in `main()` and not in `claim()`/`list_claims()`/`release()` precisely because the existing test passes `stale_after_seconds=1` directly — putting it in the library turns a repair into a test rewrite. Fixing liveness properly needs a durable owner identity (session/lane token plus heartbeat) rather than the CLI process pid, which is a redesign of the tool's ownership model, not a repair.
what_would_change_this: If some existing caller or hook invokes the CLI (not the library) with a small `--stale-after-seconds` as a legitimate recovery path, the floor would break it and would need a documented override instead — grep the repo and `.githooks/` for `work_board_claim` invocations to check. Separately, if `_owner_alive` turns out to be unreachable from `_exclusive_lock` in practice, C's delete stops being wrong, though it still would not unblock the lane.
